text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition leaders criticised by their parties after defeat in limited local by-elections held on Sunday.
- Germany permitted the Kurdish Med TV television channel to cover President Suleyman Demirel's visit, creating a diplomatic scandal.
- Coalition partners are contradicting each over on whether to issue a new Turkish lira currency.
- Organised crime boss with links to an MP and former police chief buried. His coffin was wrapped in the Turkish flag.
- Polish professor Dr. Dariuz Krzyszkowski comes to study faults causing earthquakes in the southeast Turkey.
- A report by the Turkish intelligence service confirms the relationship between organised crime, the police force and the government.
- Investors seek new address for their money after interest rates pushed down.
- Some 500 armed ring hospital to protect pro-government Kurdish tribal leader and MP who was injured in a mysterious traffic accident.
- Universities on alert for militant leftist protests on Wednesday's 15th anniversary of the founding of the Institution for Higher Education, the watchdog of universities in Turkey.
